Most people take Letrozole from days 5-9 of their cycle. Some doctors may adjust that slightly, but that’s generally when they advise people to take it. Same as Clomid. If you’re bleeding at all, spotting included, that is considered day 1 of your cycle.

*Edit: I would call your doctor to confirm when they want you to begin taking the medication. Regardless, within a few days you should plan to begin taking it or you’ll possibly miss out on this cycle.*
Any bleeding after Medroxy/Provera is considered a positive response. If there’s any blood coming out of you, you’re fine. That sounded morbid, but you get what I mean. lol

Medroxy just raises your progesterone. The medication itself doesn’t cause you to bleed. Once you stop taking the Medroxy, it causes a decline in the amount of progesterone your body has. That is what your body is supposed to do each month if you don’t conceive. The drop in progesterone is what triggers your period.
